name: badge
title: Badge
purpose: A status in a word or two, such as a task's station.
whenToUse: For the one status of an item that the reader acts on or scans for: Working, Needs input, Check failed.
Once per row of a list or table, as the row's trailing element.
Once beside the title of a view, for the status of the thing the view shows.
whenNotToUse: For facts that are not a status, such as a repository, a branch, a count or a time. Write them as plain text.
For several statuses on one item. Pick the one the reader acts on and write the rest as text. Eight or more badges outside list rows in one view fail the excess-badges rule.
For something the reader can press. Use a button or a link.
For a message with a sentence in it. Use a banner or an inline message.
As a count on an icon. Write the count as text next to a label.

variants.name: neutral
variants.use: The default, with no modifier class. A status that needs nothing from anyone yet, or has ended without a result: Queued, Cancelled, Draft.

variants.name: info
variants.use: Work in progress that needs nothing from the reader: Working, Checking.

variants.name: success
variants.use: Finished as intended: Check passed, Ready for review, Merged.

variants.name: warning
variants.use: Something the reader should know that does not stop the work: Out of date with main, Timed out.

variants.name: approval
variants.use: Waiting on the reader's answer before the work goes on: Needs input, Needs approval.

variants.name: blocked
variants.use: Stopped, and unable to go on by itself: Stopped, Rate limited.

variants.name: peer
variants.use: From another person's agent rather than the reader's own: From a peer, Peer proposal.

variants.name: tainted
variants.use: The work carries input from outside the trust boundary, such as a peer's message: Untrusted input.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: 24px tall with 12px text. It fits a dense list row without making it taller.

accessibility: Use a span. The badge is text, and a screen reader reads its words in place.
The words carry the status. The tone only supports them, so never rely on the colour, and never use a badge with an icon and no text.

An icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true". A state in the status set always takes that state's icon and tone, in every component that shows it, so the same state never appears with two icons.

The status set is a fixed table of states, icons and tones: Queued, Working, Checking, Needs input, Ready for review, Stopped, Cancelled, Check passed and Check failed. The words on the badge are the app's own, so an app may write Building for Working, but it keeps the state's icon and tone. Run status, run timeline, check list and tool call draw the same icon and tone for the same state.
Write the status in sentence case, in one to three words, in the same words everywhere the status appears.
A badge is not focusable and takes no press. When a status changes while the reader watches, announce it from a role="status" element in the view, not from the badge.

statusSet.use: Waiting for its turn. Nothing has started.
An agent or a step is running.
The work is done and its checks or a review by an agent are running.
Paused until the reader answers: an approval, a question, a decision.
Finished and checked, waiting for the reader to review the result.
Ended before it finished, by a person, a limit or the runner, and can be resumed.
Will not run or go on: superseded or withdrawn.
Ended with an error and did not finish its work.
Finished, with nothing left for the reader to decide.
The reader reviewed the result and accepted it.
The reader reviewed the result and rejected it.
